name: Tempest
s: A former diplomat uncovers a conspiracy that threatens the stability of the Korean Peninsula.

paragraphs.text: Tempest () is a South Korean spy romance television series written by Jeong Seo-kyeong and directed by Kim Hee-won. The series stars an ensemble cast led by Jun Ji-hyun and Gang Dong-won along with John Cho, Lee Mi-sook, Park Hae-joon, Kim Hae-sook, Yoo Jae-myung, Oh Jung-se, Lee Sang-hee, Joo Jong-hyuk, and Won Ji-an. It aired on Disney+ from September 10, to October 1, 2025.

The story revolves around skilled diplomat Seo Mun-ju, who served as the country's UN ambassador, and Paik San-ho, a special agent of mysterious nationality. After an army soldier kills Mun-ju's presidential candidate husband, she and San-ho try to uncover the truth behind his murder, which includes her brother-in-law. As events unfold, they are thrust into a mission to expose the truth about a nuclear crisis that threatens the stability of the Korean Peninsula.

Mike Hale from The New York Times mentioned the addition of American actors was "an improvement over the expats normally hired to play English-language roles in Asian films and series." Regarding the "soap operas at heart" aspect of Korean dramas, he stated, "the confusions of the plot and the tinniness of the dialogue are more noticeable than usual." However, Hale remarked that "the stars are attractive...the hand-to-hand combat is well choreographed and by the third episode the story starts to gain some of the juice and propulsion that we come to South Korean thrillers for." Although Tempest is officially unavailable in China, it sparked backlash among Chinese social media users, fueled by the circulation of decontextualized clips of the series. In a scene from an episode, Jun's character asks, "Why does China prefer war?" which many took to be a portrayal of China as belligerent. The depiction of the Chinese city of Dalian was criticized as presenting it as dilapidated and outdated, with scenes purportedly set there filmed instead in Hong Kong's shanty area. Another point of contention involved a red carpet with yellow five-pointed stars set in the White House Cabinet Room. In response to these controversies, TV drama critic and Professor Yoon Seok-jin of the Korean Language and Literature Department at Chungnam National University commented, "Dramas released on global OTT platforms like Disney+ are aimed at viewers around the world, so the description or expression of a specific country needs to be somewhat cautious. However, it is a natural context that various countries and past cases are mentioned in the process of dealing with the situation of the Korean Peninsula and the complex international relations of Northeast Asia.
